did_you_know.text: The phrase “a land flowing with milk and honey” is a vivid way to describe a fertile, abundant land—not rivers literally made of milk and honey.
In the ancient world, removing jewelry could express mourning, sorrow, or a temporary rejection of outward honor.
Here, the Tent of Meeting is outside the camp, unlike the Tabernacle later described as the center of God’s presence within Israel’s camp.
The Hebrew word na’ar does not necessarily mean a small child; in the Bible, it can also mean a young person or attendant.
In the Bible, “ways” often refers to a person’s conduct and character, not merely to a physical route.
The word veniflinu comes from a root meaning “to be set apart.” Moses asks that Israel be recognized by God’s presence, not only by its ancestry.
This verse expresses a central biblical idea: human beings cannot fully grasp God, so there is a limit to what people can see and understand.
The words “face” and “back” use human language to describe a limited encounter with God; they are not meant to claim that God has a human body.
